title: Check If a String Can Break Another String
summary: Determine if one permutation of string s1 can be at least as large as every character in a permutation of string s2, and vice versa, by comparing corresponding characters in both strings.
statement: Determine if one permutation of string s1 can be at least as large as every character in a permutation of string s2, and vice versa, by comparing corresponding characters in both strings.
constraints: The strings have equal length and lowercase letters.
One string can break the other when its characters can be permuted so every position is >= the other string.
hints: Sort both multisets so comparable ranks align.
Check whether every character of the first is >= its counterpart.
Also check the reverse direction with <=.
Sorted rankwise dominance is necessary and sufficient for a matching permutation by the standard exchange argument.
editorial: Sorted rankwise dominance is necessary and sufficient for a matching permutation by the standard exchange argument.

tests.explanation: After sorting, abc is componentwise no greater than axy, so xya can break abc.
The sorted comparisons cross directions, so neither string can break the other.
